vocabulary.meaning_en: the part of your face you smell with; a natural ability to find something
something bought for a low price
vocabulary.example: This coat was a real bargain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having power to change what others do
to go where no one can see
vocabulary.example: The cat disappeared under the bed.
The sun vanished behind the clouds.
I'm fond of my old teacher.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tall strong column that holds up a building
vocabulary.example: The old temple has huge pillars.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a strong piece of wood or metal fixed in the ground
vocabulary.example: He tied the horse to a post.

vocabulary.meaning_en: being sent from place to place and not given help
vocabulary.example: I got the runaround when I called the company.

vocabulary.meaning_en: saying what is wrong with someone or something
a soft hat with a peak at the front
vocabulary.example: He wears a cap in the sun.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very good; making you admire it
a statement that you are unhappy about something
vocabulary.example: I made a complaint to the manager.

fine_lines.title: Down in the dumps vs nothing to shout about
fine_lines.explanation_ar: down in the dumps تصف شعور الشخص بالحزن والإحباط. nothing to shout about تصف شيئاً عادياً غير مميز (ليس سيئاً جداً ولا رائعاً).
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Down in the dumps' describes a person who feels sad. 'Nothing to shout about' describes a thing that is just ordinary, not special.

examples.sentence: He's been down in the dumps since he lost his job.
The food was nothing to shout about.

fine_lines.title: Give someone the runaround vs from pillar to post
fine_lines.explanation_ar: give someone the runaround أن يماطلك شخص أو جهة ولا يعطيك جواباً واضحاً. from pillar to post أن تُرسَل من مكان إلى آخر دون استقرار أو نتيجة. المعنيان متقاربان.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Give someone the runaround' = not give them a clear answer or help. 'From pillar to post' = being moved from one place to another with no result. Similar meanings.

examples.sentence: The shop gave me the runaround about my refund.
I was sent from pillar to post between different offices.

expressions.meaning_en: to talk about something you know nothing about; to talk nonsense
expressions.example: He says he's an expert, but he's talking through his hat.

expressions.meaning_en: to be naturally good at finding or recognising something
expressions.example: My mum has a good nose for a bargain.

expressions.meaning_en: important or powerful people you know who can help you
expressions.example: He got the job quickly - he must have friends in high places.
She's a bit down in the dumps because of the rainy weather.
I put my keys on the table and they vanished into thin air!

expressions.phrase: have a soft spot for someone/something
expressions.meaning_ar: لديه ميل خاص / يحب شيئاً بشكل خاص
expressions.meaning_en: to like someone or something a lot, often without a clear reason
expressions.example: I have a soft spot for old black-and-white films.

expressions.meaning_ar: من مكان إلى آخر بلا استقرار
expressions.meaning_en: from one place or person to another without getting anywhere
expressions.example: My application was sent from pillar to post for weeks.

expressions.meaning_en: to avoid giving someone clear information or the help they need
expressions.example: When I asked about my parcel, they just gave me the runaround.

expressions.meaning_ar: إن كان الوصف ينطبق عليك فاقبله
expressions.meaning_en: if the criticism is true about you, accept it
expressions.example: You say people call you lazy? Well, if the cap fits!
The new restaurant is OK, but it's nothing to shout about.

grammar.title: Using 'have' in fixed expressions
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم have في تعابير عن الصفات والمشاعر: have a good nose for (موهبة)، have a soft spot for (حب خاص). بعدها يأتي for + اسم أو اسم فعل: She has a nose for finding bargains.
grammar.explanation_en: We use 'have' in expressions about abilities and feelings: have a good nose for, have a soft spot for. Then use 'for' + noun or -ing: 'She has a nose for finding bargains.'
examples: He has a good nose for a story.
I have a soft spot for cats.
She has a nose for finding good restaurants.

questions.question: 'He's talking through his hat' means he:
questions.explanation_ar: talk through your hat = يتكلم بلا علم.

questions.question: She always finds the cheapest prices. She has a good ___ for a bargain.
questions.explanation_ar: have a good nose for = لديه حاسة لاكتشاف الشيء.
questions.explanation_en: She's naturally good at finding bargains.

questions.question: He got tickets easily because he has ___ .
questions.explanation_ar: friends in high places = أصدقاء ذوو نفوذ.

questions.question: 'I'm down in the dumps' means I feel:
My pen was here a minute ago - it's ___ !
questions.explanation_ar: vanish into thin air = اختفى تماماً.

questions.question: 'I have a soft spot for my little cousin' means I:
questions.explanation_ar: have a soft spot for = يحب بشكل خاص.

questions.question: The bank ___ - nobody gave me a clear answer.
You were sent from one office to another all day. You were sent ___ .
questions.explanation_ar: from pillar to post = من مكان إلى آخر.

questions.question: 'You never help at home - if the cap fits!' means:
choices: If the criticism is true, accept it
questions.explanation_ar: if the cap fits = إن كان النقد صحيحاً فاقبله.
questions.explanation_en: If it's true about you, accept it.

questions.question: Which expression describes a THING that is just ordinary?
questions.explanation_ar: nothing to shout about = عادي غير مميز.
